title: A review axis edits, and the sweep follows the last writer

statements.says: A review axis now fixes what it finds, rather than only reporting it.
The driver takes a reading of the worktree before and after each axis step, works out what changed, and carries that to the step that reconciles.
Comment sweeping moves to the end of the loop.
The loop runs seven steps: build, standards, spec, architecture, fix, sweep, finish.
build starts the session and leaves its change uncommitted.
The three axes each run fresh, read the change, report under their own heading and may fix what they find.
fix resumes the build session and reconciles, holding all three reports and all three records.
sweep runs fresh, with no resume, and writes last.
finish resumes the build session, runs the suite, commits and closes.
Run by hand with no flag, /implement gains a reviewing section and a fixing section of its own and so mirrors the loop.
The two halves of the old finishing step are named fix and finish.
The axes are ordered: standards edits before spec and architecture read, and architecture edits after every other axis has finished.
fix and finish resume the build session, and the three axes and the sweep do not.
When axes were readers, the work was taken from the session that had the finding in hand and given to one that did not.
The driver's before-and-after reading means an edit no session announced still cannot reach a commit unnoticed.
The sweep moves to the end because every step that writes ran after its old place and could put back what it had just cut.
fix is the only step that sees the whole picture.
A sweep reading the change cold sees the whole ticket, where a sweep resumed in the build session only saw what that session had written.
fix and the suite run after all three axes, which is what makes the asymmetry of their order affordable rather than dangerous.
An axis that can only report makes the finishing step retype work already understood somewhere else.
The names fix and finish were used because Closing already means removing a worktree and its branch, and land-ticket already has a resolve step.
Keeping an axis a reader, enforced by plan permission mode or by removing the edit tools, was rejected, because fixing what it finds is the point of giving an axis a session of its own.
Having an axis name its own edits in its report was rejected, because a step written into a skill can be skipped and the driver already knows for certain what changed.
Telling a later axis what the earlier axes changed was rejected, because each axis runs fresh so that none reads another's mind, and nothing follows the last axis anyway.
Running the sweep inside the finishing step was rejected, because a step written into a skill can be skipped and a step in the script cannot, and the sweep guards a rule.

Running the sweep after the commit was rejected, because the finishing step closes the ticket, so the sweep would tidy a ticket already reported done, add a second commit and leave the suite run before the last edit.

It replaces the one sentence of the earlier record on steering rules that described the loop as sweep and review in one resumed session ending in /code-review, and the other two sentences of that paragraph stand.
